120	Now, after we have seen the Torah and the verse
121	in Ketuvim, in the book of Kohelet, let's see the Mishnah
122	in tractate Bava
123	Metsia, chapter 4 of Bava Metsia, it is written as follows:
124	If he drew the produce but did not give him the money, he cannot
125	retract. If he gave him the money but did not draw the produce,
126	he can retract. But they said: He who exacted payment from the people of the generation of the Flood
127	and from the generation of the Dispersion
128	will exact payment from one who does not stand by his word. Let's try to understand this for a moment.
129	First of all, let's learn only the topic there in the tractate Bava
130	Metsia.
131	Tractate Bava Metsia is the middle tractate between
132	two other tractates, Bava Kamma and Bava Batra. These three
133	tractates, Bava Kamma, Bava Metsia and Bava Batra,
134	make up a larger tractate called Tractate
135	Nezikin, and it deals, in fact, and this is found in the order
136	of Nezikin, one of the six orders of the Mishnah in the Talmud.
137	And these tractates deal with
138	monetary matters. In chapter 4 of Bava Metsia it speaks of
139	the system of acquisitions, how one acquires things. That is, there are
140	objects that are mine, property that is mine,
141	and the question is how an asset becomes mine or
142	leaves my possession. Now, here it speaks of two
143	people, in the discussion here
144	in the Mishnah,
145	where one sells produce to another,
146	say a greengrocer or a fruit seller
147	in the market, of course, the produce is not his, and now
148	buyers come, one comes and wants to buy. So you have to know that
149	when one buys produce, the acquisition is not made by payment of
150	money, as is commonly thought today, but rather
151	the acquisition is made by means of
152	drawing. That is, from the moment the buyer drew the thing
153	that he is buying, in this case produce, from
154	the seller's possession, he drew it, that is, he attached it to himself,
155	that is what creates the acquisition, even if he has not yet
156	paid the
157	money. Let me give an example. Picture a person
158	entering not a shop where fruit and vegetables are sold,
159	but going to buy a vase or some
160	glassware, all right? So there is the display
161	in the shop and he tells the seller, I want the
162	third vase there on the second shelf from
163	the right. The seller goes and takes down
164	this one,
165	and this vase falls
166	and breaks. Even if he paid the
167	money, the customer, as if, only needs to be brought
168	this. The payment of money does not make the acquisition until
169	the vase actually reaches his possession. That is, what
170	makes the acquisition here is
171	the drawing. Now, after more or less this principle,
172	let's see the Mishnah again: If he drew the
173	produce but did not give him
174	the money. They agreed that he buys from him, I don't know how many,
175	ten crates of oranges or apples, I don't know what.
176	And the customer drew the produce from the shopkeeper
177	and still had not given him the money, had not
178	paid him yet, he only
179	drew and did not pay the money, and afterwards he wants
180	to retract. He says, you know what, no, I don't
181	want the produce, it's not good, I'm not buying it. But he already drew it. The shopkeeper can say
182	to him,
183	sorry, you drew it, it is already yours, I am not willing to take
184	it back. This is the meaning of: he drew produce from him but did not
185	give him the money, he cannot retract. If he gave him
186	the money but did not draw the produce from him, that is, they
187	agreed that he buys these crates of oranges
188	and he already paid him the money but still did not
189	draw it, he can retract,
190	because there was no acquisition here. What is the determining acquisition?
191	It is the acquisition by drawing. Now, what happens here? To this
192	the Mishnah refers and says: But they said, He who exacted payment
193	from the people of the generation of the Flood and the generation of the Dispersion will exact payment
194	from one who does not stand by his word. That is,
195	you committed yourself, true, you have not yet performed the acquisition, but
196	you committed yourself. So by strict law you can retract.
197	But know that what is written here is a grave matter: He who
198	exacted payment from the people of the generation of the Flood and the generation of the Dispersion
199	will exact payment from one who does not stand by his word. The generation
200	of the Flood is the story that appears at the end of the book, at the end of
201	Parashat Bereshit, the beginning of Parashat Noach, right: all flesh had corrupted
202	its way upon the earth, and I am destroying them with the earth,
203	and the Flood came
204	and in fact destroyed all
205	living things. The people of the generation of the Flood were wicked people,
206	and the Holy One, blessed be He, destroyed them. Ten generations
207	later they built the Tower of Babel, this is the generation of the Dispersion, in which
208	at first the whole earth was of one language and one speech,
209	and then the Holy One, blessed be He, confounded their language, and this is called
210	Dispersion, He divided
211	them. And this punishment of the generation of the Flood and of the generation
212	of the Dispersion is the punishment of a person who does not stand
213	by his word. And here note that the Mishnah is not speaking
214	of matters between man and God, it is speaking of matters between
215	man and his fellow, of a business
216	commitment, a spoken one. So, true, apparently
217	there was no drawing here, and therefore the shopkeeper cannot
218	say to him, listen, you drew it, it's yours.
219	He can retract, but if he retracts
220	he is in fact breaking his word, breaking his promise.
221	One who breaks his promise, it is written here, something very
222	grave, that he will end up as the people of the generation
223	of the Flood and the people of the generation of the Dispersion ended up, and one must know that these matters
224	are not trivial. One must understand what happened
225	in the generation of the Flood and the generation of the Dispersion that relates to the matter of
226	not standing
227	by one's word. What all this shows us is that speech is
228	something very, very
229	serious. We came out of this, remember this whole journey,
230	we started from the verses in the Torah, the three verses in the Torah
231	in the book of Devarim in our parashah, Parashat Ki Tetzei: When
232	you vow a vow to HaShem, do not delay to pay it, and so on.
233	We saw the verses also in Kohelet, we saw now
234	this Mishnah in tractate Bava Metsia, and now let's
235	try to go a bit deeper. Perhaps let's start with the matter
236	of what is the connection between standing by one's word and the terrible punishment
237	that appears here, which is compared to the generation
238	of the Flood and the generation of
239	the Dispersion. So for this, let's go to the book of Bereshit
